::: {.why}
The curve you plotted last night is a direct measurement of how far the market's terminal distribution is from lognormal, and reading it that way makes the rest of the week straightforward.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Report the implied volatility curve for one expiry and state what its curvature says about the risk-neutral density's tails.
- Say why quoting in implied volatility rather than in price is a convention that makes the disagreement visible.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Clean and plot the chain properly: filter for quotes with real two-sided markets, invert mid prices for implied volatility using your own pricer, and plot against strike and against log-moneyness. Note that using moneyness rather than strike makes different expiries comparable, which is why everyone does it.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Read the curvature as a statement about the density: a symmetric smile means fatter tails than lognormal on both sides. Extract the implied density directly using the second derivative of price with respect to strike, and compare it against the lognormal implied by the at-the-money volatility. The two plots make the same point twice and the second is the more convincing one.
:::
:::
